references.text: Parallel verses describing the same: Israel served the Lord all the days of Joshua and all the days of the elders who outlived Joshua, who had seen all the great works that the Lord had done for Israel.
Describes the Lord's great work at the Sea of Reeds, which the people saw and which led them to fear the Lord and believe in him.
Moses exhorts the people to remember the Lord's great works that they had seen with their own eyes.
Joshua reminds the people of all that the Lord their God has done for them against all these nations on their behalf.
Describes how those who held fast to the Lord were kept alive, in contrast to those who fell away.
Moses refers to the great trials, signs, and wonders that the people had seen with their own eyes.
Contrast verses describing the next generation that did not know the Lord or the works he had done for Israel.
